questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: Introduction to C++ and program structure
questions.question: Which header file is required to use std::cout and std::cin in C++?
questions.explanation: The <iostream> header defines the standard input and output stream objects in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: Introduction to C++ and program structure
questions.question: Which operator is used with std::cout for output insertion?
questions.explanation: The stream insertion operator << inserts formatted data into the output stream.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to declare a constant integer in C++?
questions.explanation: The 'const' keyword is used to declare read-only constant variables in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the size of the 'char' data type guaranteed to be in standard C++?
questions.explanation: In C++, sizeof(char) is defined to be exactly 1.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which data type is used to store boolean values 'true' or 'false' in C++?
questions.explanation: The 'bool' keyword represents boolean logical values true or false in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the result of 17 % 5 in C++?
questions.explanation: The modulus operator % calculates the integer remainder of division (17 divided by 5 gives remainder 2).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the value of x after: int a = 5; int x = ++a;
questions.explanation: The pre-increment operator ++a increments 'a' to 6 first, then assigns 6 to x.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which scope resolution operator is used to access global variables or namespace members?
questions.explanation: The double colon :: is the scope resolution operator in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which loop guarantees that its body will execute at least once?
questions.explanation: A do-while loop evaluates its condition at the end of the iteration, ensuring at least one execution.

questions.subject: C++
questions.explanation: The assignment expression (a = 5) evaluates to 5, which is non-zero (treated as true), so "True" is printed.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the index of the first element in a standard C++ array?
questions.explanation: Arrays in C++ use zero-based indexing.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: How do you declare a 1D array of 5 integers in C++?
questions.explanation: 'int arr[5];' declares a C-style array of 5 integers.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which header file is required to use std::string class in C++?
questions.explanation: The <string> header declares std::string and std::wstring classes.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which member function returns the number of characters in std::string s?
questions.explanation: In std::string, length() and size() are synonyms that return the character count.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which keyword indicates that a function does not return any value?
questions.explanation: The 'void' return type specifies that a function returns no value.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What happens when an argument is passed by value to a function in C++?

options.A: A copy of the argument is created
options.B: The function receives the original variable address
options.C: The original variable is modified directly

questions.explanation: Passing by value copies the argument's value into the function parameter.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which symbol is used to declare a reference variable in C++?
questions.explanation: The ampersand symbol & is used to declare reference types in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which symbol is used to dereference a pointer in C++?
questions.explanation: The asterisk * dereferences a pointer, accessing the value stored at the memory address.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is a nullptr in modern C++?

options.B: A strongly-typed null pointer literal of type std::nullptr_t

questions.explanation: Introduced in C++11, nullptr is a type-safe null pointer literal.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a class in C++?
questions.explanation: The 'class' keyword defines a class type in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the default access specifier for members of a class declared with keyword 'class' in C++?
questions.explanation: Members of a class are private by default, whereas members of a struct are public by default.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the default access specifier for members of a C++ 'struct'?
questions.explanation: Struct members in C++ default to public access.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Does a constructor in C++ have a return type?

options.B: No, constructors have no return type

questions.explanation: Constructors in C++ do not specify any return type, not even void.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the correct syntax for declaring a destructor for class 'Car'?
questions.explanation: Destructors are named with a tilde ~ followed by the class name.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: How many destructors can a C++ class have?
questions.explanation: A class can have only one destructor as it takes no parameters and cannot be overloaded.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which keyword is used to establish inheritance between derived and base classes in C++?
questions.explanation: The colon : operator is used to inherit from base classes in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: In public inheritance, what access level do public members of base class have in derived class?
questions.explanation: Public inheritance preserves the access level of public base members as public in the derived class.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which access modifier restricts member visibility strictly to within its own class?
questions.explanation: Private members can only be accessed by member functions and friends of the class.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which access modifier allows visibility within the class and its derived classes?
questions.explanation: Protected members are accessible inside the class and by derived classes.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which operator is used to allocate dynamic memory on the heap in C++?
questions.explanation: The 'new' operator allocates memory on the free store (heap) and initializes objects.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which operator is used to deallocate dynamic memory allocated with 'new[]' for arrays?
questions.explanation: Array dynamic memory allocated with new[] must be freed using delete[].

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: STL containers (vector, list, deque, set, map, unordered_map)
questions.question: Which STL container header provides std::vector?
questions.explanation: <vector> defines the std::vector dynamic array container.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: STL containers (vector, list, deque, set, map, unordered_map)
questions.question: How do you add an element to the end of std::vector<int> v?
questions.explanation: push_back() appends an element to the end of a vector.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: STL containers (vector, list, deque, set, map, unordered_map)
questions.question: Which method checks if an STL container has zero elements?
questions.explanation: v.empty() returns true if the container has no elements, equivalent to checking size() == 0.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which block is used to enclose code that might throw an exception in C++?
questions.explanation: The 'try' block encloses code that may trigger runtime exceptions.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which keyword is used to signal/raise an exception in C++?
questions.explanation: The 'throw' statement raises an exception in C++.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: How is a static member variable initialized outside the class definition in C++?
questions.explanation: Static member variables are defined at namespace scope using scope resolution: Type ClassName::memberName = value;

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Can a static member function access non-static instance variables of the class directly?

options.B: No, because static member functions do not have a 'this' pointer

questions.explanation: Static member functions lack a 'this' pointer and can only access static members or instance objects passed explicitly.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which standard algorithm sorts elements in a range [first, last) in C++?
questions.explanation: std::sort from <algorithm> sorts elements in a given range.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Which output stream object is used for unbuffered error reporting in standard C++?
questions.explanation: std::cerr is the standard unbuffered error output stream.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What does 'auto' keyword do when declaring a variable in C++11 and later?

options.B: Deduces the variable's type automatically from its initializer

questions.explanation: In modern C++, auto enables compile-time type deduction based on the initialization expression.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the result of expression: 5 + 3 * 2 in C++?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher operator precedence than addition, so 3 * 2 = 6, and 5 + 6 = 11.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is a base condition in a recursive function?

options.A: The line where recursive function calls itself
options.B: The terminating condition that stops recursion

questions.explanation: The base condition stops further recursive calls and prevents call stack overflow.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the result of string concatenation: std::string a = "Hello "; std::string b = "World"; std::string c = a + b;
questions.explanation: The + operator concatenates std::string objects, producing "Hello World".

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What statement exits immediately from a loop or switch statement in C++?
questions.explanation: The break statement terminates execution of the nearest enclosing loop or switch.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is function overloading in C++?

options.A: Defining multiple functions with the same name but different parameter lists in the same scope
options.B: Redefining a base class function in a derived class
options.D: Passing too many arguments to a function

questions.explanation: Function overloading allows functions in the same scope to share a name if their parameter signatures differ.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element in an array or std::vector by index?
questions.explanation: Random access by index in contiguous arrays takes constant time O(1).

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: Can a C++ reference be rebound to refer to a different object after initialization?

options.B: No, references are bound permanently upon initialization

questions.explanation: A reference cannot be rebound to another object after its initialization.

questions.subject: C++
questions.question: What privilege does a friend function have regarding a class in C++?

options.A: It can access private and protected members of that class
options.C: It becomes a member function automatically

questions.explanation: Friend functions are granted full access to private and protected class members.

questions.subject: C++
questions.topic: Introduction to C++ and program structure
questions.question: What is the return type of the main() function in C++ standard?
questions.explanation: According to C++ standards, main() must return int.
